story: On a sunny Tuesday morning at 8:17, with the Florida air already warm at 77 degrees, Gary heads down Magnolia Loop with a hopeful spring in his step. Donna is packing her pickleball bag at home, making sure there are paddles, balls, and a spare grip ready for doubles practice with Gary. Meanwhile, Hal sits at his kitchen table with his violation notebook, determined to strike anything the rules don't cover and keep only the L-01 and L-02 items. Rosa, content in her kitchen, checks what's left in the pantry and starts planning the next batch of food for the neighbors.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Pack paddles, balls, and a spare grip for doubles practice with Gary
Hal (hal violation notebook): Go through the entries, strike anything the rules don't cover, keep only L-01 and L-02 items
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check what's left in the pantry and plan the next batch of food for the neighbors

gary.thought_process: I've already soldered the speaker wiring and bench-tested the light strings indoors, and the cart is untouched while I wait on Architectural Review approval. Nothing left to do at the bench. It's 8:17 AM, sunny, and I'm alone at home. Rather than puttering around and letting the quiet get to me, I'll head over to the Architectural Review desk to check whether my form has been looked at yet, since the approval is what's holding up the parade project. Staying honest with the neighborhood means asking, not sneaking.

parameters.content: Heading out to check on the status of my golf cart modification form with Architectural Review.

donna.thought_process: It's a bright Tuesday morning and I'm home alone. Gary and I are on the ladder as Pruitt-Kowalski, and last tick I penciled in a practice, but I haven't checked where Gary actually is since dinner at Rosa's. Time to put the plan into motion: grab my pickleball bag so I'm ready to head to the courts, and keep the calendar in mind so I stay within the two-hour reservation limit. Then I can track Gary down and get him moving.

parameters.content: Pack paddles, balls, and a spare grip for doubles practice with Gary

hal.thought_process: Dinner at Rosa's went fine and I'm forgiven. Morning now, nobody around. In my last tick I resolved to review the notebook and only note what the rules actually cover. L-01 and L-02 are the real rules. I want my entries clean before I take anything to the committee, and I want my own cart mod approval pressed too. Better to tidy the notebook now than go off half-cocked.

parameters.content: Go through the entries, strike anything the rules don't cover, keep only L-01 and L-02 items

rosa.thought_process: The welcome dinner at my table seems to have come together already, with Hal and Donna pitching in last tick. It's Tuesday morning and I'm alone at home. I just checked my per-diem schedule, so now I should look at the kitchen and plan the next dinner. Prepping ahead is the practical thing to do, and it keeps the table warm and ready for the neighbors I want around it.

parameters.content: Check what's left in the pantry and plan the next batch of food for the neighbors

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
